question: Can an existing public regulatory QA harness be extended with version chains and target-date labels, or must the version-level benchmark pipeline be built from scratch?
description: A public regulatory-document QA harness with structure-aware chunking and sparse/dense/hybrid arms exists, but its corpus is static with no document versioning or target dates, so it cannot test temporal gating as-is. It is unclear whether that harness can be extended with version chains and target-date annotations at acceptable cost, or whether the benchmark pipeline must be built from scratch on an amended legal corpus.
rationale: Reusing a verified harness would cut implementation cost substantially, but its corpus has no amendment relations, so extension may require replacing the corpus and the label pipeline entirely.
